title: Cross-Block FlashMerge: hybrid attention handoff with prefetch compression and KV warmup
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces Cross-Block FlashMerge attention kernel with prefetch compression and KV warmup. Improves p50 latency and throughput for long-context workloads. No public API changes. Opt-in behind runtime flag --attn-crossblock-flashmerge.
description: Context: long-context workloads and mixed-size batches reveal inefficiencies in block-local attention kernels: boundary handoff between tiles forces repeated loads and prevents KV cache warm paths from being effective. Motivation: reduce cross-block memory traffic and enable early KV warmup while preserving numerical parity and compatibility with existing rotor/rope encodings. This PR implements a hybrid execution strategy called Cross-Block FlashMerge that splits attention computation into two cooperating phases: local-block compute (fast, Flash-optimized) and a lightweight handoff phase that merges partial results across neighboring blocks. The design also adds a prefetch-compression step for rotary/rope embeddings to reduce memory bandwidth when streaming long sequences, and a proactive KV warmup path that populates small warm KVs for expected next tokens using a cheap predictive sampler. Key features: 1) FlashMerge kernel: new CUDA kernel that fuses q,k,v GEMM + scaled-dot + softmax + out projection for intra-block work while exposing a compact handoff envelope for inter-block reduction; 2) Cross-block handoff: small fixed-size metadata buffers exchanged between adjacent tiles to avoid reloading full KV slabs; 3) Prefetch compression: lightweight delta-encoded rotary/rope transform that reduces per-token bandwidth for long sequences by ~2x with negligible compute overhead; 4) KV warmup: scheduler hook that issues background warmup requests for recently seen conversation prefixes; warm KVs are retained in the LRU hotset until eviction pressure; 5) Scheduler integration: continuous-batcher updated to honor handoff-aware batching windows and to start warmup for small-latency targets. Performance summary: microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge, fp16, sequence length 8k: end-to-end throughput +27% vs baseline flash-attn, median latency (p50) down 18% at batch size 1 for 2k contexts, peak GPU memory reduced by ~6% on hot-paths. Accuracy: numerical differences are within 1e-5 of the previous Flash kernel for fp16 accumulation; no quantization regressions observed in our eval harness. Safety and compatibility: feature is gated behind runtime flag --attn-crossblock-flashmerge and kernel selection policy prefers proven flash variant for small sequence lengths. Rolling deploy plan: canary on Dedicated first (10% traffic), collect trace-level latency and rand-eval quality metrics for 48h, then phased rollout. Tests and validation: unit tests for kernel math, deterministic small-sequence validation, integration bench harnesses added, end-to-end regen tests for chat service. Notes: runtime knobs exposed: attn.crossblock_enabled (bool), attn.prefetch_compression (enum: none|delta), attn.kv_warmup_window (int). How to review: focus on kernel correctness (tests in tests/kernel/), scheduler interactions (scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp), and perf regression risks in mixed small/large workloads. Related: ENG-1284 (attention scheduling), ENG-1299 (kv cache hotset).

review_threads:
Ben Hollis: Can you explain why we need the handoff buffer format rather than simply concatenating partial reductions? Please add a short comment in flashmerge_kernel.h, and include a size/alignment note.
Aisha Kapoor: Added comment and alignment table in flashmerge_kernel.h; handoff buffer keeps 64B metadata per tile to avoid atomic ops across SMs.

Priya Natarajan: Scheduler changes look invasive for the continuous-batcher. Did you measure impact on small-sequence throughput (<=128 tokens)?
Aisha Kapoor: Yes, we ran mixed-traffic microbenchmarks; small-sequence p95 latency saw <2% regression in worst-case. Added opt-out path for small sequences and a unit test in tests/bench/ to validate. Updated PR with results and graphs.

Luca Moretti: Prefetch compression seems heuristic. How robust is it to variable rotary scales? Any precision loss?
Aisha Kapoor: Prefetch compression is delta-encoding of rotary phases and uses a fallback to full representation if variance exceeds threshold. We added unit tests to exercise extreme scales; numerical diff <1e-5 in fp16 accumulative tests.

CI Bot: gpu-integration (flaky) failed on first run (OOM in long-seq smoke).
Aisha Kapoor: Reduced temporary buffer footprint, added guard to avoid launching flashmerge for sequences below min_tile_size. Reran CI; passed.
